scope: One-process request-capture preload for the existing Mercury HTTPS client and existing CLI. Diagnostic only.
guidance_refresh: No differences from previously verified guidance at a0f613297097e70095835baad299f85e4be4f3be in root/full AGENTS, Mercury README, config, exclusions or rules.

helper_attempts.setup_warning: The sandbox PATH lacks rg. Tool execution was synthetic; no grep was attempted and no fallback was used.

limitations: Synthetic transport only; no provider/TLS/server behavior exercised.
Capture records client write/end bytes, not proof of remote receipt.
No historical request10 reconstruction or Mercury review clearance.

mechanics: The preload imports only Node built-ins and reads the nonsecret canonical mercury.config.json. It does not import the application before the CLI loads dotenv.

Only the exact configured Mercury HTTPS POST object-form request is captured. The original request receives unchanged arguments, options and callback; request.write/end receive their original arguments and return their original result.
Request bytes are saved as received by the diagnostic boundary, never parsed and reserialized by the preload. No headers are read or retained.
Private packet/request-capture-* directories are 0700. Exact request bodies and the metadata event journal are 0600. Request bodies are never printed by this preload or its new verification mode.

Response data is hashed in an additional listener; existing response consumers and createProviderAudit/writeRawProviderOutput continue. The response SHA, ordinal, PID and timestamps correlate the private request to its existing raw audit.
New capture directories and files use exclusive creation; existing packets and the prior serialization receipt remain preserved.
proposed_neutral_question: What value does startLivenessWatchdog assign to broker in the pinned runner? Cite the assignment line.
limits: Only the current actual-client one-write/no-end-body path and synthetic response delivery were exercised. No claim is made for all Node overloads, TLS bytes, socket backpressure timing, or remote receipt.
Synchronous file writes and hashing add diagnostic overhead. Filesystem failures propagate visibly, as the existing audit writer does; there is no silent fallback capture.
If the process terminates or the response aborts, a missing request_end_called or response_ended record means incomplete capture, not an empty successful request or response.
The historical request10 body is still unavailable. This does not establish the cause of its inc_tool_call output or clear Mercury.
The original fixture raw-body display remains its preexisting synthetic-only mode; --verify-request-capture prints hashes and booleans without request bodies.

The original offline fixture observation made no live provider call or production/client/config/hook change. A later parent-authorized live source lookup is recorded separately in source-lookup-receipt.json.
This public-safe curation contains hashes, metadata, synthetic assertions and limitations only. It does not copy private request JSON, raw response contents, or private log contents.
